ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an operational amplifier comparator, with input u_i connected through resistor R to the inverting terminal (marked “-”); the non-inverting terminal (marked “+”) is directly connected to the fixed reference voltage given in the figure, labeled 17.2 V; the output terminal is u_o. Reasoning: The ideal op-amp input terminals take no current, so no voltage drop is produced across resistor R due to op-amp input current, and the inverting-terminal voltage equals the input u_i. At the threshold, the op-amp differential-mode input is zero, i.e. v_- = v_+. Therefore the input threshold voltage U_T is equal to the reference voltage connected to the non-inverting terminal, namely 17.2 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: u_i enters the inverting terminal through R, while the non-inverting terminal is connected to the fixed reference voltage shown beside it. Since the op-amp input draws no current, the resistor does not shift the inverting-terminal voltage. At the threshold, set the differential input to zero, v_- = v_+. Therefore U_T is simply the reference voltage connected to the + input; reading that label gives U_T = 17.2 V.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct comparator-threshold route: identify the op-amp input connections and use the equality of the two input terminal voltages at the switching point. It is the natural single solution path for this simple circuit.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit as an inverting-input comparator: the signal input is applied through resistor R to the op-amp − terminal, the + terminal is tied to the fixed reference source shown at the lower left, and the output is labeled u_o. The reference label at the + input is the threshold-setting voltage, corresponding to 17.2 V in the source figure.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to identify the requested quantity as the threshold voltage U_T in volts; all circuit values and topology come from the figure.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal op-amp comparator, input current is negligible, so there is no voltage drop across the series input resistor at threshold. The switching threshold occurs when v_- = v_+, hence the input threshold equals the non-inverting reference voltage.
